lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine's biggest conference job in 2024 wasn't giving a talk. It was making sure nobody hit a broken PDF link in a hallway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: GraphQuon, the Quebec and Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop for East-Canadian computer graphics labs. The 2024 edition ran November ninth and tenth at ÉTS in Montréal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what's the point of a pre-SIGGRAPH event?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Students present work headed for SIGGRAPH to a friendly but constructively critical audience, and get feedback before the real submission crunch. Labs take turns hosting, and 2024 was ÉTS's turn.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So Antoine was on the organizing side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, the web side. He helped build and host the site on GitHub Pages, with schedule pages and contact blocks. He says it taught him the boring critical path: bios on time, links that don't 404, and a schedule that works on a phone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine had a hallway chat with Masha Shugrina from NVIDIA. She showed Diffusion Texture Painting from SIGGRAPH 2024, where a diffusion brush paints on a mesh so strokes stay seamless. Plus a Gaussian splat scene you could walk around in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He called it the useful kind of industry chat, concrete tools instead of buzzwords.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the questions were about evaluation and whether a method would survive a SIGGRAPH reviewer, not startup pitches.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's a nice follow-up too. In 2025 he presented at the Toronto edition, and he says organizing first made presenting calmer. He already knew where the HDMI adapter lived.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Funny how the unglamorous job pays off. The full write-up has the schedule highlights and tips for next year.
